diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, when $\tau$ is large, the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

H_1^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) - \theta \cdot (x - x_0)),\ H_2^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) + \theta \cdot (x - x_0)),\ H_3^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) - \theta^{\perp} \cdot (x - x_0)),

issues.failure_explanation: With a=t-t_0, y_1=theta.(x-x_0), y_2=theta^perp.(x-x_0), the product v_0 v_1 v_2^2 = H_1 H_2 H_3 = tau^{3/2} exp(-tau/2 (l_1^2+l_2^2+l_3^2)) with l_1=a-y_1, l_2=a+y_1, l_3=a-y_2, and l_1^2+l_2^2+l_3^2 = 3a^2+2y_1^2+y_2^2-2 a y_2, not 2(a^2+y_1^2+y_2^2) as claimed. The quadratic form has determinant 4, so tau^{3/2} \int q exp(-tau/2 v^T M v) dv -> q(x_0,t_0) (2 pi)^{3/2} / sqrt(4) = sqrt(2) pi^{3/2} q(x_0,t_0). Hence the boundary integral tends to 3! sqrt(2) pi^{3/2} q(x_0,t_0), and the stated formula is off by the factor sqrt(2) ~ 1.41.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace pi^{3/2} by sqrt(2) pi^{3/2} in eq: recoequ pw (equivalently, correct the claimed product approximation to the anisotropic Gaussian and recompute the normalization). No change to the method, its convergence, or the Radon reconstruction is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise reconstruction formula eq: recoequ pw is miscalibrated by a factor sqrt(2); the implemented pointwise reconstructions (the comparison remark and the unregularized pointwise algorithm with its figures) inherit the amplitude error. The Radon reconstruction formula and method are unaffected.
issues.title: Pointwise reconstruction formula has an incorrect normalization constant (missing factor sqrt(2))
issues.why_classification: A one-constant correction obtained by a direct Gaussian-integral recomputation; the pointwise method, its convergence, and all other claims are preserved, so no substantive content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$, and defining
For the numerical solution of the forward problem we use the parameters $N_{x_1} = N_{x_2} = 80$ and $N_t = 1500$ in the space domain $\Omega = [-0.5, 0.5]^2$ and time domain $[0, T] = [0, 3]$.
$P$ corresponds to the interval $[-0.4, 0.4]$ divided into $63$ equally spaced distances from the origin.

issues.failure_explanation: The reconstruction identity requires the auxiliary wave v_0 = H_2^{tau,(t_0,theta_0,eta_0)} to vanish together with its time derivative at t=T throughout Omega (eq: wave v_0); this holds only if the support of H_2(.,T), namely {x: x.theta_0 in [eta_0+t_0-T-h, eta_0+t_0-T+h]}, avoids Omega, i.e. t_0 < T - eta_0 - r - h for max_{x in Omega} x.theta_0 up to r. With r = sqrt(1/2) ~ 0.7071, T = 3 and the implementation's choice t_0 = T/2 + eta_0, the condition becomes eta_0 < T/4 - r/2 - h/2 ~ 0.396 - h/2. For the last sinogram row eta_0 = 0.4 (and angles near the diagonals, where max_{x in Omega} x.theta_0 > 0.7), it fails: the support intersects Omega, v_0 != H_2, and the reconstruction identity is unjustified for that row.

failure_location.quote: More specifically, for each $\eta_0 \in P$, we set the auxiliary function $v_0$ corresponding to $(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0)$ as in Section \ref{sec: choosing boundary for radon}. With these choices, we can reconstruct $\radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0) = \radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\theta_0, \eta_0)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict P to [-0.39, 0.39] or choose t_0 per eta_0 inside the admissible window (eta_0 + r + h, T - eta_0 - r - h); the method and advertised scope are otherwise unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The reconstructed sinogram row eta_0 = 0.4 for near-diagonal angles is computed outside the causal/admissible region, so its values (and the filtered backprojection images, slightly) are not justified by the reconstruction theory. All other rows are unaffected.
issues.title: Sinogram construction uses t_0 = T/2 + eta_0 outside the admissible region for the last distance row
issues.why_classification: A single boundary row of the sinogram lies marginally outside the admissible parameter regime; a local restriction of the parameter range repairs it with no loss of method or conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all examples, the noisy measurements are simulated by adding Gaussian noise with standard deviation

issues.failure_explanation: With noise standard deviation sigma_0 = sigma * mean|Lambda_q(eps_1 f_1)| and sigma = 0.02, the standard amplitude signal-to-noise ratio of the measurements is 20 log10(1/sigma) = 20 log10(50) ~ 34 dB (equivalently 10 log10(1/sigma^2) ~ 34 dB), not approximately 44 dB; 44 dB would require sigma ~ 0.6% or a nonstandard peak-based SNR definition, which the paper does not state.

failure_location.quote: We use the noise level $\sigma=2\,\%$ in all our examples. This results in a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $44\,\mathrm{dB}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the SNR to approximately 34 dB under the stated noise model, or specify the SNR definition (e.g. peak-to-noise) that yields 44 dB.
issues.overall_effect: Only the quantitative description of the experimental noise level; the reconstruction methods and results are unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed signal-to-noise ratio of 44 dB is inconsistent with the stated 2% noise level
issues.why_classification: A one-number correction or a definitional clarification; no mathematical content is lost.
